gates.note: The semantic address oracle is gone from every prefetch path: cache_sim defaults to an address-only, confirmation-gated, region-bounded stream detector with a finite in-flight budget, and the oracle survives only as a labelled upper bound. Measured on web-Google PageRank the oracle's advantage is 19-31x more cost-free prefetch requests but only +5.1% (P-OPT) and +2.0% (LRU) demand misses. The gate stays PENDING because fills remain synchronous and free: a prefetch completes before the demand that triggered it, with no lateness, bandwidth contention or real MSHR occupancy. Timing-bearing prefetch evidence must come from gem5.
Under STRIDE8 K2 converts demand misses into ~1.36x total traffic and ~1.67x prefetch fills. A demand-miss metric does not price this.

cache_sim now issues P-OPT's rereference-matrix column stream as real non-temporal accesses with explicit two-column residency, so it is priced through the hierarchy rather than as a flat post-hoc charge. Measured on web-Google PageRank the flat charge erred in both directions: it added 229,108 demand misses under STRIDE8 where the true cost is 2,413, and it counted a single sweep where a two-iteration run streams 458,240 lines. The gate stays PENDING because the stream is modelled on the ordinary demand path and is therefore covered by cache_sim's prefetcher, whereas published P-OPT uses a dedicated streaming engine writing into the reserved ways and disables conventional prefetching; total_memory_traffic also excludes LLC writebacks.

A fresh, non-resumed run of the provenance-bound Pin 4.2/GCC 13 compatibility port reproduces the qualitative public-artifact direction: P-OPT has fewer raw demand LLC misses than DRRIP on all four PageRank graphs. This is not an exact Pin 2.14/GCC 6.3 reproduction, speedup evidence, P-OPT-vs-GRASP evidence, validation of GraphBrew's internal P-OPT model, or a K2 ranking.

On three DBG-reordered, one-sweep PageRank samples, the receipt-bound 4-byte compact K2-I implementation reduces DRAM traffic and LLC misses versus the 8-byte implementation at tied instruction count. Timing is a single-core TimingSimpleCPU serialized ISA-model result with uncalibrated compact-decode latency; it is not measured hardware timing, O3 scale, an all-algorithm result, or a replacement-policy ranking.

Primary metrics (execution time + total off-chip traffic), the decision rule, aggregation, admissibility and symmetry requirements are declared before the deciding experiments and enforced by scripts/test/test_frozen_metrics.py.

K2's structural bypass (StreamShield) was available to K2 alone; every other policy was returned a no-bypass transport. The option is now offered to every policy via --structural-bypass, and every row records which setting was used. Measured on web-Google PageRank the bypass is worth -20.0% to LRU, -5.0% to GRASP and -1.7% to P-OPT against StreamShield's -2.4% to K2, and with it equalised K2+StreamShield loses to LRU+bypass.
